text:
maria: Heads-up: a customer flagged weird SSE lag. Console showed repeated route penalty and a reconnect, but backend logs show steady writes. Client tcpdump shows client RX window collapsing before each stall.

kevin: Interesting. So proxy thinks there's no acks, but client is advertising zero-ish window? That would make proxy backpressure the root cause, not our runtime.

maria: Exactly. Snippet from client: `rcv_wnd=65535 -> rcv_wnd=0 -> stall 5s -> rcv_wnd=65535` repeated. Proxy increments penalty on perceived stalled ack interval and triggers sticky-routing fallback. Client reconnects when app times out.

tara: How are we currently distinguishing network-level backpressure (client window) vs proxy-induced stalls? I thought we looked at `last_ack_ms` + `tokens_emitted`. We don't yet surface rcv_wnd in console.

kevin: We don't sample TCP window size in telemetry. We assumed ack timing was sufficient. But if client is slow-reading, ack arrives but window=0 so proxy can't send more and thinks it's stalled.

maria: Proposed fix: enrich route telemetry with `tcp_rcv_wnd_series` (sampled 1s) and a derived `client_limited` flag when avg_rcv_wnd < threshold for Xs. Use that to suppress route penalty and mark the flow as client-limited.

tara: UX: console should show "client-limited" overlay and explain why route wasn't throttled (or was). Otherwise SRE keeps chasing our runtime.

kevin: Security/privacy: capturing raw window sizes is low risk. But do we want to store series at 1s resolution long-term? Maybe keep it as ephemeral metric and surface aggregates (percentiles) to console only for last 5m.

maria: Implementation plan: 1) proxy agent samples TCP rcv_wnd per connection every 1s and emits metric `conn.tcp_rcv_wnd.p50` and `conn.tcp_rcv_wnd.p10`. 2) routing decision uses `client_limited=true` if p10 < 8192 for >3s. 3) console displays mini histogram and flags. 4) add a per-route config `client_limited_grace_ms`.

tara: Tests needed: simulate slow reader (zero window) and verify we don't penalize route; also simulate proxy pause (no writes) to ensure penalty still triggers.

kevin: Also add a small diagnostic CLI: `ri stream-debug --conn-id <id>` that prints latest tcp_rcv_wnd_series so oncall can triage quickly.

maria: Rollout: canary proxy v2 with tcp sampling -> alpha hosts 5%. Telemetry off by default. We'll enable for affected tenants first.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: routing-proxy/tcp-rcv-sample v2 -> canary group alpha (5%). ETA 13:00 UTC.

tara: One more thought: mobile clients might naturally have tiny windows due to radio power cycles; we should ensure default grace is generous (10s) to avoid false positives.

kevin: Good call. Make default client_limited_grace_ms = 10000, and tenant override if they want stricter policy.

maria: I'll open PRs for proxy sampling, routing check, console overlay, and runbook update. Will paste links here. TL;DR: root cause = client-side read-window collapse -> proxy sees stall -> route penalty. Fix = surface tcp_rcv_wnd and make routing window-aware.
